variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: From the batch HGVS: missense (NP_000202.3:p.(Gly251Ser)). Table S2 gives type 'Missense', Exon 7, domain 'VWFA'. Mechanism in the paper is general: the LFA-1 alpha subunit is not expressed without the beta subunit. Cohort-level: 89% of VWFA-domain variants gave absent CD18 on neutrophils.

quotes.quote: | | VWFA | c.751G\>A | p.Gly251Ser | Exon 7 | Missense | *P23#P63#,P72#, P73#, P74#* | rs179363873 |
It is known that α- subunit of LFA-1 cannot be efficiently expressed unless it first associates with the β subunit.
Out of the total mutations identified in the VWFA domain, 89% of them resulted in absent expression of CD18 on PMNs causing severe infection in LAD1° and LAD1^- cases.

concerns: Single source: a multicentre retrospective cohort (Kambli 2020, PMID 33391282); per-person genotypes come only from Supplementary Table S2, which gives no transcript and no genomic coordinates.
The paper says 30 of its patients were reported before in its ref 18 (Madkaikar 2015, PMID 25703682) without naming them, so carriers here may be the same people as in that paper.

Table S2's '#' marks are inconsistent: P23, P63 and P76 carry one '#'-marked and one unmarked variant, 12 patients are '#'-marked in all, while the text says compound heterozygous variants were found in only 10 patients.
No parental or family testing is described for LAD1 (the family-testing sentence in the methods refers to NGS for LAD3); Table S1 has a Family History column but no genotyped relatives.
P23: this variant is '#'-marked but the second variant listed for P23 (c.1878-2A>C) is not.
P63: this variant is '#'-marked but the second variant listed for P63 (c.1658-2A>G) is not.
P74's Table S1 row is cut off in the converted text after the organisms cell (ANC and outcome missing).

Five carriers, each '#'-marked and each with a different second ITGB2 variant (P23 c.1878-2A>C, P63 c.1658-2A>G, P72 c.1283T>G, P74 c.2147G>T, P73 c.742-1G>A); the second variants for P23 and P63 are not '#'-marked. P23, P72 and P74 link to candidates G-lad1-008, G-lad1-029 and G-lad1-001.
P63 is LAD1+ in Table S1, contradicting the text's statement that compound heterozygous variants were seen only in LAD1° cases.
Table S2 gives the same rs number (rs179363873) for this variant and for c.715G>A (p.Ala239Thr); one of them is likely a transcription error in the paper.
Whether any of the five are related is not stated; P72, P73 and P74 are all from consanguineous families per Table S1, which sits oddly with compound heterozygosity.
Table S2's references column gives an rs number rather than 'Novel'.
notes_for_panel: All evidence comes from one multicentre Indian cohort (PMID 33391282): genotypes from Supplementary Table S2, clinical rows from Supplementary Table S1. No segregation, de novo, phase or variant-level functional data are reported; the CD18 flow-cytometry subtype is the only per-person laboratory finding. Zygosity is per-person only through Table S2's '#' marks, which are inconsistent.
